transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because my mind keeps going blank at the worst times. I’ll be looking at the road-closure forms or holding the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I can’t remember the steps I’ve done for years.
When your mind goes blank like that, about how long does it typically last?
It can last a few minutes, sometimes longer. I just stand there looking at the forms or holding the paddle, trying to remember what I’m supposed to do.
Outside of these episodes, have you noticed any problems with your memory or thinking in daily life?

Yes. Even when I’m not right in the middle of one, I feel like my thinking isn’t as sharp. I can look at the road-closure paperwork or hold the stop-slow paddle and just... not be able to remember the steps I’ve done for years.
How has your mood been feeling recently?
Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow sadness in my chest. It feels like the day is already ruined before I even get out of bed.
Have you ever experienced a period in the past where you felt this down or depressed?
Yes. I’ve felt this kind of depression before—waking up with that heavy, hollow feeling, like the whole day is already ruined before I even get out of bed.
Did your memory problems start around the same time you began feeling this sadness?

I’m not sure exactly when they started together, but the blanking out has been happening enough that it’s why I came in. I’ll be looking at the road-closure forms or holding the paddle, and suddenly I can’t remember steps I’ve done for years.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in the things and activities you normally enjoy?
Yeah. I used to organize choir rides, garden swaps, even snacks for the youth basketball games. Now I just sit for hours staring at my phone and don’t feel like answering anyone or doing any of it.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn't worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
…Yes. I keep thinking it might be better if I just didn’t wake up. I don’t have the energy to fight that thought anymore, and I’ve started saying it out loud. It scares my family.
Have you been feeling down on yourself, such as feeling worthless or excessively guilty?
Yes. I keep going over all the little things I didn’t do—for my friend, the choir, my family. It makes me feel useless, like I deserve whatever punishment is coming.
Are you currently still able to work, or has this made it impossible for you to do your job?

I haven’t been able to do my job reliably. I get stuck on the road-closure paperwork and I don’t trust myself to remember the traffic-safety steps. I’ve pulled away from work, choir, volunteering—my family finally felt like they had to bring me in for help.
How have your energy levels been recently?

My energy is very low. I used to organize choir rides, garden swaps, even snacks for the youth basketball games. Now I can sit for hours just staring at my phone and I can’t make myself answer anyone.
How has your sleep been recently?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I haven’t been paying close attention to my sleep.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite recently?
Yeah. Food just doesn’t mean much to me lately. I skip meals without really noticing, and my flagger pants have gotten loose. My family keeps saying I look drawn.
